hypothesis: Bounded canonical single-block map/reduce loops can be split before whole-loop canVectorize or VPlan construction. Independent integer-add and ordinary float/double-add reductions consume original contributions from private bounded scratch. An explicitly safe scalar helper without a vector mapping can keep the producer scalar while normal LV vectorizes the consumer. Arithmetic-only producers and one or multiple reductions use the same transformation; there are no pressure, chain-depth, reduction-count or original-vectorizability prerequisites.
semantics: The original guarded preheader, scalar producer instruction order, canonical IV and exit branch remain. A sibling consumer clones each original reduction update, IV increment and exit comparison, retaining initial values, operand order, grouping, flags, wrap semantics and exported final values. It consumes exactly the same participating iterations in order. Only canonical zero-start/unit-step IVs and eq/ne tests of next versus an invariant bound are accepted. SCEV must prove an exact count and finite constant maximum; checked unsigned layout arithmetic and the existing scratch ceiling bound storage. Narrow IVs are zero-extended for scratch addressing. A use check rejects accumulator feedback and all non-final-reduction live-outs. Original memory accesses must be simple read-only loads; scratch is new and private, so no noalias assumptions or guards are introduced. Direct scalar calls require memory(none), nounwind, willreturn and speculatable and reject convergence, noduplicate/nomerge, returns_twice, tail calls, strictfp and operand bundles. No libm-name inference, errno relaxation or extra fast-math flags. Constrained operations and strictfp functions are rejected. The early path never adds reassoc and retains normal LV hint contracts. Stage markers prevent scalar or VPlan refission. SE forgets the enclosing nest and block dispositions; LI is updated, DT recalculated, and loop-access caches cleared before the stages enter the ordinary worklist. Executable coverage added to llvm/utils/check-reduction-fission.py and reduction-fission-execution.c.in asserts actual scalar-producer/vector-consumer IR, checks both settings of the separate fission FP option, and inserts host-only vector-consumer entry probes after header PHIs. Exact integer and ordered float/double comparisons cover zero, one, odd/tail, maximum, rejected-by-entry-guard, aliased input/output, and narrow constant-count cases. RVV code generation/machine verification and host fixed-vscale execution remain separate. No build, compiler, test runner or execution checker was run by this worker.
costs: One static entry alloca per distinct contribution, deduplicated by SSA identity. Capacity is the proven maximum, execution traffic uses actual N. For each distinct contribution of allocation size S, there are N*S bytes of stores and N*S bytes of loads; multiple sums of the same SSA contribution reuse the consumer load. Scalar-helper fixture: capacity 65, 260 scratch bytes, 8*N traffic bytes. Arithmetic i64 fixture: 520 scratch bytes, 16*N traffic bytes. Mixed four-reduction/three-slot fixture: 65 i32, double and float elements, 1044 layout bytes including 4 bytes alignment padding, 32*N traffic bytes. Constant narrow case: 800 bytes for 200 i32 elements; one-iteration case: 4 bytes. Original input reads/helper calls are not duplicated or reread, and there is no producer recomputation. The loop control is repeated, and normal LV can add its usual tail/iteration checks independently. No new alias/SCEV guard or recursive pass machinery is added. The scratch ceiling is per candidate; multiple candidate loops in a function can have multiple entry allocations. Legality is linear in instructions/uses plus existing SCEV analysis; emission uses maps for distinct contributions and exported updates, and a full dominator recalculation. No new profitability model; scalar-stage overhead or lack of measured speedup is not treated as a legality rejection.
limitations: Implementation and tests await independent harness compilation and execution; no passing-test, benchmark-coverage or speedup claim is made. No RVV target execution was performed. General CFG, conditional reductions, early exits, masked participation, noncanonical IVs/tests, multiple-add recurrence chains, non-add reductions, intermediate/old-accumulator live-outs, writes, volatile/atomic loads, indirect calls, read-only-memory calls, tail calls and operand-bundle calls remain unsupported by this initial scalar path. Only float/double ordinary FP reductions are accepted; no constrained/strict FP transformation or fission-option reassociation is implemented here. Existing normal-vectorizer hint permissions are unchanged; ordered execution tests explicitly disable hint reordering. Nested single-block loops use the same LI/SE updates, but no new nested execution fixture was added. The executable consumer probe changes only host test IR; uninstrumented RVV IR is separately submitted for machine verification. Low-count and weak-producer loops may gain overhead because no profitability model is introduced.
evidence: Read BENCHMARKS_ANALYSIS.md and frozen SWIFT t000002 / LibSVM t000016 source/check evidence, plus the immutable base revision and existing implementation. The 117 original benchmark inputs remain untouched. The frozen examples motivate pre-legality stage splitting but have CFG/call-contract limitations; no claim is made that their libm calls satisfy this initial safety contract.
test_expectations: Existing reduction-fission lit RUN lines and the legacy execution fixtures explicitly set -enable-scalar-reduction-fission=false to continue testing VPlan pressure selection, forced stage VF pairs, scratch combination, FP policy isolation, and their original golden output. No existing correctness check or expected result was removed. The new scalar path defaults on only under the existing reduction-fission enable flag, and has dedicated positive/rejection/limit/fixed-VF/double-invocation tests. New executable fixtures explicitly exercise that default early path; forced normal LV width makes consumer execution deterministic and is not an implementation legality prerequisite.
future_work: After independent validation, consider small CFG participation support, additional simply structured recurrence updates, and a separately proven read-only-call contract. Validate nested-loop execution and target runtime behavior before claiming those measurements. Capacity-bounded tiling could reduce whole-trip scratch for larger loops, but is not implemented.
